title: Incident Triage Facets and Operator Mental Model Catalog
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document defines a compact, repeatable mental model for platform operators to use when triaging LLM inference incidents, describes a small set of curated dashboard facets (views) that support those mental models, and provides an onboarding checklist + rollout procedure for making new dashboards live with adequate alerts and operator training. The goal is to reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) and mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for multitenant inference degradations while keeping alert noise under control.

Audience
--------
- Platform operators (primary)
- SRE/Platform engineers maintaining runtime and telemetry
- Product/PMs who consume latency/cost SLOs
- Oncall engineers for Dedicated/Hosted clusters

Operator mental model (high level)
--------------------------------
We use a 4-facet triage mental model: Latency, Availability, Cost/Token economics, and Output Quality. Each facet maps to specific telemetry, common root causes, and operator actions. When receiving an alert, the oncall should first identify dominant facet(s) before drilling into services.

1) Latency facet
- Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 server-side request latency, connection queue depth, GPU scheduling wait time, HTTP2 stream stalls
- Typical causes: tail queuing, kernel contention, cold KV cache misses, backend dependency slowness (embeddings/reranking), cross-region routing
- Quick checklist: confirm scope (single tenant vs many), verify kernel-switch events in runtime logs, check recent kernel/quantization rollouts, inspect GPU utilization and host-level load averages
- Suggested alert thresholds: p95 > 300ms for model-small routes, p99 > 1.5s for latency-sensitive routes

2) Availability facet
- Primary signals: error rates (4xx vs 5xx split), request timeout counts, active instance count, deployment health probe failures
- Typical causes: model crash, OOM on hot path, eviction due to spot preemption, service mesh sidecar failure
- Quick checklist: correlate error type (OOM/connection reset) to service logs, confirm replica health and recent autoscaler events, check for node preemption or kernel panic events
- Suggested alert thresholds: request_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m on high-criticality routes

3) Cost / Token economics facet
- Primary signals: token throughput (tokens/s), per-token cost estimate, unexpected embedding call fanout, batch size distribution changes
- Typical causes: prompt amplification from client changes, request storm from a single tenant, disabled batching or prefetching, misconfigured model variant routing (swap to larger, costlier model)
- Quick checklist: inspect tenant token breakdown, recent changes to client SDK versions, routing policy changes, Batching service queue lengths
- Suggested alert thresholds: tenant token usage spike > 5x baseline over 10m or per-token cost delta > 3x expected

4) Output Quality facet
- Primary signals: downstream eval regressions (synthetic checks), model hallucination score for known prompt-sets, customer-reported quality signals, post-embedding similarity drift
- Typical causes: model version rollout, quantization artifacts, prompt template regressions, data-plane truncation/cutoff errors
- Quick checklist: identify recent model/quant rollout, reproduce failing prompt set in regression lab, check truncated token counts and KV cache miss rates
- Suggested alert thresholds: quality-regression-alarm when >10% of regression tests fail on canary traffic

Dashboard facet catalogue (minimal set)
------------------------------------
Each facet is represented by a small dashboard 'facet' view. Dashboards must be concise (<= 8 panels) and provide a deterministic path to the first operator action. Panels should reference exact query IDs used by the operator library.

A) Latency Facet - "Latency Facet :: Service Lens"
- Panels (examples):
  - Global p50/p95/p99 (PromQL): sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route) -> convert to percentiles
  - Queue depth over time (PromQL): avg_over_time(platform_queue_depth[10m]) by (pool)
  - GPU scheduling wait time (custom metric): runtime_gpu_sched_wait_ms
  - Recent kernel-switch events (logs link): button linking to Kusto query id: runtime_kernel_events_last_30m
- Owners: runtime-team / eng-platform-telemetry

B) Availability Facet - "Availability Facet :: Error Split"
- Panels:
  - 4xx vs 5xx rates by route (PromQL): sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"4..|5.."}[5m])) by (status_class, route)
  - Timeouts and retries (derived metric): request_timeout_total / request_total
  - Replica health heatmap: per-node replica_count and probe_failure_count
  - Recent pod OOM/killed events (k8s events link)
- Oncall action buttons: run emergency model swap, scale-to-safety (runbook link)

C) Cost Facet - "Cost Facet :: Token Economy"
- Panels:
  - Tenant token rate + top-5 tenants (PromQL): sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (tenant) topk(5, ...)
  - Per-token cost estimate (derived): running_cost_estimate / tokens_emitted
  - Batch size distribution histogram (runtime metric): batch_size_bucket
  - Route-level model variant shifts (annotation layer): shows deploy metadata
- Automated mitigations: soft-rate-limit tenant with excessive token surge (operator approval button)

D) Quality Facet - "Quality Facet :: Regression Canary"
- Panels:
  - Canary regression pass rate (synthetic suite)
  - Example failed prompt traces (link to trace view)
  - Per-model hallucination metric over last 24h
  - Canary vs baseline token length distribution
- Oncall workflow: trigger immediate canary rollback or escalate to applied-ml-and-evals

Dashboard engineering requirements
--------------------------------
When creating facet dashboards follow these rules: 
- Keep the total panels <= 8 per facet.
- Every panel must include a single-line operator note (why it exists, what an anomalous shape means).
- Anchor each dashboard with 2 quick action buttons: (1) Link to the primary runbook for the facet, (2) Owner contact/rotation schedule.
- Provide an annotations layer for deploys and runtime kernel switches.
- Add synthetic control traces for end-to-end verification (for every route marked SLO-critical).
- Tag dashboards with labels: facet:<latency|availability|cost|quality>, owner:team-slug, release:YYYY-MM-DD

Runbook wiring and alerting guidance
----------------------------------
- Alert grouping: Alerts must be grouped by tenant OR route depending on scope. Use the following conservative defaults: if >25% of requests across tenants affected, group by route; if <25% affected, group by tenant.
- Alert severities mapping: SEV0 - production outage affecting >3 regions or >15% of traffic; SEV1 - high SLO burn for >15 minutes; SEV2 - intermittent or small SLO burn; SEV3 - informational or investigation alerts.
- Alert deduplication: Use indexed fingerprinting with primary keys (route, tenant, cluster) and suppress alerts if the same fingerprint flaps more than 3 times in 10m unless severity escalates.
- Pager duty playbook: attach the facet runbook and the last 24h facet dashboard view to the pager notification payload.

Onboarding checklist for new facet dashboards
-------------------------------------------
1) Draft dashboard in staging with owner and docstring for each panel.
2) Add synthetic queries and verification traces for at least 2 representative routes.
3) Define at least 2 alert rules derived from dashboard panels (one for detection, one for escalation).
4) Run tabletop with 2 operators and one PM for the route; capture 3 playbacks.
5) Fill the dashboard metadata page with owner rotation and runbook links.
6) Publish to prod with a 48-hour monitor-only period.
7) After 48 hours review false positives and adjust thresholds.

Rollout procedure for replacing legacy dashboards
-----------------------------------------------
1) Create a migration branch: replicate current legacy panels into the new facet but keep them disabled.
2) Run the new facet in parallel for 72 hours, collecting operator feedback in the migration doc.
3) Replace alert targets to notify a closed review channel (do not page) for the first 24 hours after cutover.
4) If no regressions, flip to live paging and deprecate the legacy dashboard with a 30-day tombstone period.

Operator training and cognitive aids
----------------------------------
- Maintain a 1-page mental model card for each facet (PDF) stored alongside the dashboard. Cards must include: primary signals, three likely root causes, three first-responder commands/queries.
- Monthly 45-minute lab exercises: one simulated latency surge, one token storm, one canary regression.
- Create a pocket cheat sheet CLI wrapper: `redwood-observe triage --facet latency --route X` that yields the 6 canonical queries for the facet.

Retrospective guidance and improvement loops
------------------------------------------
- For every SEV1/SEV0 incident where MTTM > 30m, capture which facet was dominant and whether the facet dashboards provided the needed context.
- Maintain a lightweight incident improvement backlog: every retrospective must produce 1 owner + 1 measurable experiment (example: reduce false-positive rate for p95 alert by adding queue-depth panel).
- Quarterly metric: fraction of incidents resolved within the first facet-identified action should be > 65%. Track in the platform health dashboard.

Appendices
---------
A. Example queries and notes (operator-friendly)
- Top-10 tenants by token rate (PromQL): topk(10, sum by(tenant) (rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])))
- p95 calculation pattern (helper query): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- GPU wait time anomaly: increase > 2x baseline in runtime_gpu_sched_wait_ms_over_1m

B. Ownership matrix (single-line table)
| Facet | Primary owner | SLA reviewer | Runbook folder |
| Latency | runtime-team | eng-platform | /runbooks/latency-facet |
| Availability | eng-sre | runtime-team | /runbooks/availability-facet |
| Cost | platform-cost | finance-legal | /runbooks/cost-facet |
| Quality | applied-ml | product | /runbooks/quality-facet |

C. Fast rollback safety checklist (for model swap)
1) Confirm canary traffic routing is working and historical canary pass rate baseline.
2) Take snapshot of current variant mapping and persist.
3) Trigger swap to baseline model variant with grace period; monitor canary regression panel for 10m.
4) If regressions drop, follow full rollback runbook.
